title: Multi-source in-transit visibility fusion for contested movement (RFID, satellite trackers, carrier EDI and manifests into a trusted COP that survives disconnected legs)

scores.rationale: FACT/HIGH: USTRANSCOM itself solicited a prototype to 'ingest, fuse and visualize' tracking sources into a trusted COP (CSO AoI 001, posted 2026-05-20, grantedai.com mirror) and GAO/DoDIG have documented the shortfall since 2006 (GAO-06-366R; GAO-13-201, 2013-02; DoDIG-2014-058, 2014-04-11; GAO-17-183, 2017). Not a 5 because the pain is chronic and tolerated: analysts have lived with phone/e-mail chasing and slide-built COPs for two decades, which shows it is survivable in peacetime.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: every DoD movement generates heterogeneous reads and every contested/austere/allied-port leg goes dark; DDOC and 618th AOC watch floors work the problem daily and exercises (Valiant Shield 24, Turbo Fusion 25/26) keep re-surfacing it. Acute frequency is highest in contingency/exercise rather than routine CONUS moves, so not a 5.

Score of 1 explained: no discrete RDT&E or procurement line for ITV fusion was found in the study's FY2026 sweep (E05-F30; card labels this HYPOTHESIS/LOW); IGC sustainment is understood to run on USTRANSCOM's Transportation Working Capital Fund/O&M (RECALL - not re-verified this session), and the only sized figure is the ~$27M D&G sustainment task order (orangeslices.ai, 2025-03), which is a services contract to someone else. CSO AoI 001 funding size is undisclosed. Only reason it is not 0: the CSO/OT vehicle exists and DIU's JSDT lane shows adjacent joint-logistics money is being obligated (diu.mil, 2026-02-19).

FACT/MEDIUM: the USTRANSCOM base CSO is standing (reported open to 2036, bwcoconsulting.com) and OT/CSO has no statutory ownership test (E07-F22), which is a real door. But the only specific ITV AoI closed 2026-06-04 with no public award four months later (all three skeptics re-searched 2026-09-25), the buyer is single (USTRANSCOM/DLA), and the program office is effectively the IGC sustainer's task order. Path PROBLEM->USER->REQUIREMENT OWNER->PROGRAM OFFICE->CONTRACTING OFFICE is identifiable (DDOC users; J3/J5 owner; J6/IGC; TCAQ) but the BUDGET link is missing and the VEHICLE window is closed, so a major penalty applies.

INFERENCE/HIGH: probabilistic multi-source track association, entity resolution across identifier schemes (TCN/container/tag/PRO-BOL), dead-reckoning route models and store-and-forward edge reconciliation are mature techniques from ISR track fusion and commercial visibility (project44/FourKites-class do carrier-EDI/telematics fusion at scale). The hard part is data access and identifier hygiene, not the algorithm. Not 5 because trust-scoring carrier EDI without ground truth is an unsolved evaluation problem.

FACT (card capital table)/MEDIUM: $250k covers only the synthetic-data proof of concept (card: 150k-300k); a credible military demo is 1.0-2.5M and is realistic only if a CSO/OT award funds it. The founders could reach a simulation, not a demo a buyer would act on.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: a synthetic Turbo Fusion-like replay is buildable in 3-6 months, but a demo that is credible to USTRANSCOM requires real CUI feeds via CRADA/exercise slot, which the card places at 12-18 months and which is gated on a sponsor the founders do not have; the next exercise cycle (Turbo Fusion 2027) is the earliest realistic proof point.

Score of 1 explained: everything that matters (IGC/GDSS extracts, TC-AIMS II/GATES/IBS manifests, actual RFID and mesh reads, Turbo Fusion exercise data) is CUI on NIPR/IL4-IL5 held by USTRANSCOM, D&G and LMI, and per the card is 'not obtainable without a sponsor'. Only open AIS/ADS-B and X12 EDI specifications are available, which lets the team prove algorithms on synthetic data but cannot validate the actual claim that fusion beats last-read under real feed conditions (card mvp.what_it_must_prove). E07-F30: CUI access for a foreign national is constrained by contract and export controls.

FACT/MEDIUM: ITV data is predominantly CUI, not classified, and the OT/CSO route has no ownership test (E07-F22) - materially easier than kinetic C2. Offsetting burdens: NIST 800-171/DFARS 7012 and CMMC Level 2 posture from the first CUI-bearing pilot (E07-F9/F11), IL4/IL5 hosting and RMF ATO or inheritance, a technology control plan for the Indonesian non-U.S.-person co-founder, and DoDI 5205.87 FOCI review at production scale (E07-F20). Describes constraints only; counsel needed, not a legal judgment.

FACT/HIGH: the card rates classification dependence 'eventually'; the MVP can be built entirely on open AIS/ADS-B, licensable X12 EDI specs and synthetic RFID/mesh generators, and pilots are CUI rather than classified. Not 5 because OPSEC-sensitive unit movements and ITAR-controlled manifest details can pull real deployments into restricted handling.

FACT/MEDIUM: LMI NADACS/SPECTR is exercise-validated by AMC (Valiant Shield 2024; 400+ cargo pieces in Turbo Fusion late 2025; platform launched Dec 2025, washingtonexec.com 2025-12); D&G holds the IGC sustainment scope (~$27M, awarded 2025-02-28); Savi controls the RFID-IV/aRFID-V hardware and data formats; Booz Allen runs Pegasus/Advana analytics; Palantir's Army EA ($10B ceiling, cnbc.com 2025-08-01 - ceiling, not revenue) gives DoD-wide reach; project44/FourKites hold the commercial fusion IP (no verified DoD contract - Public evidence insufficient). Five-plus credible responders to a single buyer.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: incumbents are dashboard-and-hardware oriented and none is positioned as a source-agnostic fusion layer, and mesh tags currently feed a separate silo rather than IGC - a real seam. But the vulnerability is easily closed: USTRANSCOM can task D&G inside the existing IGC task order or CDAO can add an Advana workload, and the card's own defensibility section concedes 'the algorithms alone are reproducible by Palantir/LMI'.

Score of 1 explained: the card lists eight interface owners (IGC via D&G/TCJ6/DLA; Pegasus/Advana via CDAO; GDSS via AMC/618th AOC; TC-AIMS II/GATES/CMOS/IBS via the services; Savi RFID formats; LMI mesh gateways; carrier EDI gateways; TAK) and states 'the startup controls none of them'; IGC API specifications are CUI and available only via sponsor. Adapter work per source plausibly exceeds the fusion core, which pushes the business toward integration services. Not 0 only because EDI, AIS/ADS-B and CoT/TAK are open standards.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: durable advantage would come from an ATO inside the IGC/Advana boundary, built adapters and exercise-validated performance - but those are single-customer, non-transferable assets, and the algorithmic core is reproducible by well-resourced incumbents. Data-network effects (the commercial moat of project44-class firms) do not accrue to a vendor of one government customer.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: DDIL-tolerant, trust-scored multimodal shipment fusion is reusable for humanitarian relief, mining/energy remote supply chains and allied militaries (card rates 'medium'), but the mainstream commercial visibility market is already served by far larger data networks, leaving the differentiated part as a niche.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: one U.S. buyer; allied extension (NATO JSEC/JLSG, Bundeswehr) improves the story but runs into coalition data-releasability policy a startup cannot fix, and EDF eligibility is lost if U.S.-incorporated. The only credible expansion is lateral re-use of the fusion engine for other DDIL track-fusion problems, which is a different gap, not growth within G20.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: if inserted inside IGC or Advana the natural model is recurring sustainment/subscription funded from working-capital/O&M, which is repeatable but low-margin and services-shaped; with a single customer and a prototype-stage market ('Prototyping' per card; S14 'Transitioning' at the ITV edge), there is no evidence yet of a recurring software buy for fusion.

Score of 1 explained: the card marks a former USTRANSCOM/AMC/SDDC ITV subject-matter expert and a multi-source fusion engineer as both 'fatal_if_absent'; two university students have neither, no USTRANSCOM relationship, and no way to obtain CUI feeds. The Indonesian non-U.S.-person co-founder faces technology-control-plan and (at scale) DoDI 5205.87 FOCI friction on exactly the CUI transportation data the product depends on, and SBIR is closed by the >50% U.S.-person ownership rule (E04-F30). The strong engineer could build the fusion core, and the German founder's Bundeswehr/NATO network is a modest allied asset, which is why this is 1 not 0.

market.summary: Single buyer (USTRANSCOM/DLA); the only ITV procurement door (CSO AoI 001) closed 2026-06-04 with no public award by 2026-09-25; no discrete budget line (IGC on working-capital/O&M, CSO award sizes undisclosed, study note HYPOTHESIS/LOW); LMI is the exercise-validated likely awardee; interface captured by D&G's ~$27M IGC task order and Savi hardware formats; 20 years of GAO/DoDIG findings show an institutional (tagging, EDI validation) rather than algorithmic failure; identifier chaos pushes the work toward integration consulting; near-term TAM in the low-single-digit millions.

competition.summary: LMI NADACS/SPECTR is a fielded, AMC-validated (Valiant Shield 2024), 400+-cargo-piece (Turbo Fusion late 2025), commercially launched (Dec 2025) multi-source ITV stack from a firm with USTRANSCOM relationships; D&G can be tasked to add fusion inside IGC; Savi controls the RFID/Iridium data layer; Palantir (Army EA, $10B ceiling) and Booz Allen (Pegasus/Advana) can absorb fusion as a workload; a separate SBIR topic (ITV blockchain, RECALL/LOW) shows government funding its own alternative; SBIR ownership rule and CUI/TCP friction apply to the Indonesian co-founder.

feasibility.summary: Fails on access (all real data is CUI behind an incumbent sustainer), timing (AoI 001 closed 2026-06-04, likely to an exercise-incumbent), institutional cause (GAO 2006-2021 plus DoDIG-2014-058 show untested EDI and tagging discipline, which software cannot fix), commercial proof-by-absence (project44/FourKites/Tive have no verified DoD ITV contract), integration cost (8 interfaces the startup controls none of; credible demo at $1.0-2.5M is 4-10x founder capital), MVP ceiling (synthetic demo proves only algorithms), regulatory (TCP for the non-U.S.-person founder; DoDI 5205.87 at production scale) and defensibility (algorithms reproducible by Palantir/LMI).

verdict_rationale: Three independent skeptics refute at strengths 4, 4 and 5, and the Gap Evidence Card's own killer_risk and incumbent_response sections already conclude 'reject as a standalone company thesis'. I concur and cannot rebut them with evidence: the decisive reason is that the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE chain is identifiable (DDOC/618th AOC users; USTRANSCOM J3/J5 owner; J6/IGC; TCAQ) but the chain breaks at BUDGET (no discrete line found; IGC on working-capital/O&M - RECALL/LOW; CSO award size undisclosed) and at CONTRACT VEHICLE (the only specific ITV AoI closed 2026-06-04 and, per searches on 2026-09-25, no award is public; the next opening is unknown). This is a single buyer whose data interface (IGC, sustained by D&G under a ~$27M task order awarded 2025-02-28), hardware layer (Savi RFID-IV/aRFID-V) and exercise track record (LMI NADACS/SPECTR at Valiant Shield 2024 and Turbo Fusion 2025/26) are all held by others, and whose real feeds are CUI that two students cannot see without a sponsor. Twenty years of GAO/DoDIG findings (GAO-06-366R 2006 through GAO-21-125 2021; DoDIG-2014-058) locate much of the shortfall in tagging compliance and unvalidated carrier EDI - governance problems a fusion engine does not fix. Market attractiveness 2.4 and founder fit 2.2 are both below a survivable threshold, and founder fit is dragged down by two 'fatal_if_absent' roles the team lacks plus CUI/FOCI friction for the non-U.S.-person co-founder. Where the skeptics overreach: the persistence of GAO findings does not prove the problem is unfixable by software (the AoI 001 language explicitly asks for fusion), and absence of project44/FourKites DoD contracts is weak evidence either way. Neither point rescues the thesis. The narrower versions the skeptics propose (portable fusion engine for blue-force/DDIL track fusion, or subcontractor to an AoI 001 awardee) are not narrower forms of G20 - they are different gaps or a services relationship - so the verdict is 'kill' rather than 'borderline', with the technical wedge flagged for re-use under an adjacent gap. Confidence MEDIUM: the one fact that could reopen this is a public AoI 001 outcome, which remains 'Public evidence insufficient'.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (verdict is kill). For the record, the only survivable derivative is not a G20 company: build the source-agnostic probabilistic track-fusion / entity-resolution / disconnected-edge reconciliation engine as portable IP and aim it at an adjacent lane with an open door and named sponsor (DIU/INDOPACOM blue-object management, Army NGC2 data-layer apps, or an allied logistics customer via the German founder's Bundeswehr/NATO JLSG network), while offering the engine as a licensable component to whichever prime (LMI, D&G or an AoI 001 awardee) ends up inside the IGC interface. Re-score that as its own gap if the study wants to pursue it.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today they should NOT build a USTRANSCOM ITV company, and here is why the sequence fails at every step. What they would build first: a synthetic-data fusion engine and thin COP (probabilistic association of RFID, mesh/Iridium, EDI 214/315 and manifest events into confidence-scored shipment tracks, with dead-reckoning across outages and a store-and-forward edge node), buildable in 3-6 months for roughly $150-300k. Who they would show it to: USTRANSCOM J3 (DDOC) or the J6 CSO lead, AMC A4 (which ran the Valiant Shield 24 and Turbo Fusion trials) and DLA Troop Support. What the demo would prove: on synthetic ground truth, that fusion beats a naive last-read baseline on location error and time-to-detect divergence, and that edge and enterprise nodes reconcile after a 24-72 hour disconnect. Why the customer would care: the card's evidence shows they do care - USTRANSCOM wrote 'ingest, fuse, visualize' into CSO AoI 001 (2026-05-20). But the demo cannot prove the thing the customer actually needs to see, which is performance on real IGC/EDI/RFID feeds, because those are CUI held by D&G, LMI and USTRANSCOM and the founders have no sponsor, no ex-DDOC/618th AOC logistician (a 'fatal_if_absent' role) and a co-founder whose access to CUI transportation data would need a technology control plan reviewed by counsel. Why an incumbent can crush them: USTRANSCOM can task D&G to add fusion inside the existing ~$27M IGC task order, LMI already has hardware-plus-dashboard exercise history across two cycles and a December 2025 commercial platform, CDAO can stand up the same logic as an Advana/Pegasus workload, and the only 2026 solicitation window closed on 2026-06-04 with no public award as of 2026-09-25, so the founders would arrive after the door shut at a buyer that would then have a prototype and no need for a second. The milestone that would justify the next $2-5M - a signed CRADA or CSO/OT award granting real CUI feeds plus a named DDOC/AMC champion and an exercise slot (Turbo Fusion 2027) where the engine measurably outperforms last-read on government-owned ground truth - is precisely the milestone the founders cannot reach with $250k, no sponsor and no insider, which is why the honest answer is to redirect the engineering effort into the same fusion core under an adjacent gap with an open, named door rather than spend the capital here.
bear_case_summary: Single buyer; only ITV procurement window closed 2026-06-04 with no public award (searched 2026-09-25); no discrete budget line (HYPOTHESIS/LOW); data interface (IGC/D&G ~$27M task order), hardware layer (Savi) and exercise track record (LMI NADACS/SPECTR, Valiant Shield 24, Turbo Fusion 25/26) all held by others; real feeds are CUI unobtainable without a sponsor; 20 years of GAO/DoDIG findings show largely institutional causes (tagging compliance, unvalidated carrier EDI); eight interfaces the startup controls none of; credible demo costs 4-10x founder capital; team lacks both 'fatal_if_absent' roles; non-U.S.-person co-founder faces TCP/FOCI friction; algorithms reproducible by Palantir/LMI.
bull_case_summary: The pain is real and government-acknowledged in the customer's own words (CSO AoI 001 'ingest, fuse, visualize', 2026-05-20); the base CSO is a standing vehicle open for years and OT/CSO has no ownership test (E07-F22); ITV is CUI not classified, so the MVP starts fully unclassified on open AIS/ADS-B and EDI specs; incumbents are dashboard/hardware oriented and mesh tags currently feed a silo outside the system of record, leaving a genuine fusion-layer seam; cheap mesh/Iridium trackers multiply heterogeneous feeds and make fusion more valuable; DIU's JSDT lane (prototype OTs Jan and Jul 2026) shows new entrants can win adjacent joint-logistics work; the fusion core is reusable for humanitarian, remote-industrial and allied logistics and for other DDIL track-fusion problems.
